Reproductive Health – Problems and Strategies
subtopics: Reproductive and Child Health Care (RCH) Programmes
Awareness and Sex Education in Schools
key_concepts: Reproductive health means total well-being in physical, emotional, behavioural, and social aspects of reproduction.
RCH Programmes focus on creating awareness, providing medical facilities for pregnancy, delivery, STDs, contraception, and maternal/child health.
Amniocentesis is a foetal sex-determination and genetic disorder detection technique (Down syndrome, haemophilia) legally banned to prevent female foeticide.

modules.title: Population Stabilisation and Birth Control Methods
subtopics: Population Growth Trends & Reasons for Explosion
key_concepts: Population explosion is driven by a rapid decline in death rate, maternal mortality rate (MMR), and infant mortality rate (IMR), alongside an increase in the reproducible age group.
An ideal contraceptive must be user-friendly, easily available, effective, reversible, with least side-effects, and non-interfering with sexual drive.
Natural methods (periodic abstinence, withdrawal, lactational amenorrhea) rely on avoiding ovum-sperm meeting without devices.
IUDs (Lippes loop, CuT, Cu7, Multiload 375, Progestasert, LNG-20) suppress sperm motility, increase phagocytosis, and make the uterus unsuitable for implantation.

modules.title: Surgical Methods and Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP)
subtopics: Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) and Legal Status
key_concepts: Vasectomy involves removing or tying up a small part of the vas deferens through a scrotal incision, blocking sperm transport.
Tubectomy involves removing or tying up a small part of the fallopian tube through an abdominal or vaginal incision, blocking ovum transport.
MTP was legalised in India in 1971 with strict conditions to prevent illegal female foeticide and misuse.
MTP (Amendment) Act 2017 permits termination within 12 weeks on one doctor's opinion, and 12-24 weeks on two doctors' opinions for specific health/foetal abnormality grounds.

modules.title: Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs) and Prevention
subtopics: Definition and Alternative Names (STI, VD, RTI)
Transmission Routes and Complications (PID, Ectopic Pregnancies)
Prevention Principles and High-Risk Age Groups
key_concepts: STIs (Sexually Transmitted Infections) or VDs (Venereal Diseases) or RTIs (Reproductive Tract Infections) are transmitted through sexual intercourse.
Common STIs include Gonorrhoea, Syphilis, Genital herpes, Chlamydiasis, Genital warts, Trichomoniasis, Hepatitis-B, and HIV/AIDS.
Hepatitis-B, Genital herpes, and HIV are incurable; most other STIs are completely curable if detected early and treated properly.
Complications of untreated STIs include Pelvic Inflammatory Diseases (PID), abortions, stillbirths, ectopic pregnancies, infertility, and reproductive tract cancer.

modules.title: Infertility and Assisted Reproductive Technologies (ART)
subtopics: Infertility Definition and Causes (Physical, Congenital, Immunological)
In Vitro Fertilisation (IVF) and Embryo Transfer (ET)
ZIFT (Zygote Intra Fallopian Transfer) and IUT (Intra Uterine Transfer)
GIFT, ICSI, and Artificial Insemination (AI / IUI)
key_concepts: Infertility is the inability to produce children despite 2 years of unprotected sexual cohabitation.
In Vitro Fertilisation (IVF) involves fertilisation outside the body in simulated laboratory conditions, followed by embryo transfer (ET).
ZIFT transfers zygote or early embryo (upto 8 blastomeres) into the fallopian tube; IUT transfers embryos with >8 blastomeres into the uterus.
Artificial Insemination (AI / IUI) introduces semen from husband or healthy donor into the vagina or uterus to overcome low sperm counts or insemination failure.

modules.title: Comprehensive NCERT End-of-Chapter Exercises & Board Masterclass
key_concepts: Abortions can happen spontaneously (miscarriages) as well as induced (MTP).
Infertility is not solely due to female abnormalities; it can equally involve the male partner or other biological factors.
Surgical methods prevent gamete transport, not gamete production.
